segments.expected: She read that over. It was longer than anything in the green pages; it had cost her a summer, and it went into nine lines.
segments.transcript: She read that over. It was longer than anything in the green pages. It had cost her a summer, and it went into nine lines.

segments.expected: Went wrong: opened the second door before the first was shut. Three times. That is a stack. It is soft, and it costs a third of the price, and it lands. It is also two doors open together, and open to anything that is near. I am forbidden it, and I was right to be.
segments.transcript: Went wrong, opened the second door before the first was shut, three times. That is a stack. It is soft, and it costs a third of the price, and it lands. It is also two doors open together, and open to anything that is near. I am forbidden it, and I was right to be.

segments.expected: She could not write the fold; it was not hers. She had learned it off a first-year on a pail, and did it with two fingers stuck out like a fork; and when she tried to put down what the hands did, she found that she was describing Pru's.
segments.transcript: She could not write the fold, it was not hers. She had learned it off a first year on a pail, and did it with two fingers stuck out like a fork. And when she tried to put down what the hands did, she found that she was describing Pruse.

segments.expected: She could not write the second gap either.
segments.transcript: She could not right the second gap either.

segments.expected: The first was only dear, and one paid for it. The second came, each time, out of somewhere that had already been emptied, and something paid all the same, and it went out through her left arm; she had felt it pass the wrist. That was not a method. It was a thing that had happened to her three times and that she did not understand.
segments.transcript: The first was only dear, and one paid for it. The second came, each time, out of somewhere that had already been emptied. And something paid all the same, and it went out through her left arm. She had felt it past the wrist. That was not a method. It was a thing that had happened to her three times, and that she did not understand.

segments.expected: Pump house, about one. M.R.'s reading hand starved to the wrist. Eased by Aske with 1.2 of our sealed W. A.R. held the comb: plain. Lumb's book for 2604, one leaf, to be kept; see M.R.
segments.transcript: Pump house, about one. MR's reading hand starved to the wrist. Eased by ASCII with one. Poo about seal W. AR held the comb. Plain. Lum's book for Toonie 604. One leaf, to be kept. See MR.

segments.expected: "Pryce. Cade. Renn. Rowan." She did not look up. "I've been an officer of this company for eleven years. I've never had a card come back with a team written on it. I don't know that there's a column."
segments.transcript: Price, Cade, Wren, Rowan. She did not look up. I've been an officer of this company for 11 years. I've never had a card come back with a team written on it. I don't know that there's a column.

segments.expected: "There wasn't one for before, either," said Pike.
segments.transcript: There wasn't one for before either, said Pike.

segments.expected: He was by the stove, in the open door of the mending room, with a purse sheet across his knees. He had a needle in his right hand. Kiva saw him shut the hand on it twice, slowly, as a man works a stiff glove, before he set a stitch.
segments.transcript: He was by the stove in the open door of the mending room as the purse sheet across his knees. He had a needle in his right hand. Kiva saw him shut the hand on it twice, slowly as a man works a stiff glove before he set a stitch.

segments.expected: She went in. Kiva heard her boots on the iron stair.
segments.transcript: She went in. Kiva heard her boots on the iron stair.

segments.expected: Pru had come, since the card said Finch. She stood at Kiva's shoulder with a hank of waxed cord round her wrist, and she was already making turns on it, small and quick, without looking.
segments.transcript: Prue had come, since the card said Finch. She stood at Kiva's shoulder with a hank of waxed cord round her wrist, and she was already making turns on it, small and quick, without looking.

segments.expected: "Stop that," said Pike. "No. Don't stop. Do it again."
segments.transcript: Stop that, said Pike. No, don't stop. Do it again.

segments.expected: Pru had gone on making knots the whole time. She did not drop one.
segments.transcript: Prue had gone on making knots the whole time. She did not drop one.

segments.expected: "I told you he'd not like it." She looked rather pleased. Then she looked at Kiva's left cuff, which had come undone, and did it up without a word.
segments.transcript: I told you he'd not like it. She looked rather pleased. Then she looked at Kiva's left cuff, which had come undone, and did it up without a word.

segments.expected: Mrs. Pryce could not send her home, since Kiva had been in and out of that laundry from the age of nine, and had been fed there.
segments.transcript: Mrs. Price could not send her home, since Kiva had been in and out of that laundry from the age of nine and had been fed there.

segments.expected: She wrote, small, in the corner of the ticket: Same as P.F.'s ward. Then she went on looking.
segments.transcript: She wrote, small, in the corner of the ticket. Same as P.S. Ward. Then she went on looking.

segments.expected: It was not that she had forgotten; one did not forget it. But she had not let herself look straight at it since the night in the pump house, with three pumps going and a calf book open under a desk lamp.
segments.transcript: It was not that she had forgotten, one did not forget it, but she had not let herself look straight at it since the night in the pump house, with three pumps going and a calf book open under a desk lamp.

segments.expected: She had been thirteen the first time, and it had come again in the spring, on Classification Day, with a fever after it, and once more in the Pit, in the fifth month. There had been no roof. That was the part that she could never get said properly, even to Mara: it was not that the roof was gone and one saw the dark. There was nothing over her at all, and the nothing was not empty. It was enormous, and it was paying attention.
segments.transcript: She had been thirteen the first time, and it had come again in the spring, on classification day, with a fever after it, and once more in the pit in the fifth month. There had been no roof. That was the part that she could never get said properly, even to Mara. It was not that the roof was gone and one saw the dark. There was nothing over her at all. Then nothing was not empty. It was enormous, and it was paying attention.

segments.expected: A woman had written that down, lifetimes ago, in a house on a hill, and a pump keeper had written it in 2604, in brown ink, with his needles standing up. Not dark. Nothing.
segments.transcript: A woman had written that down, lifetimes ago, in a house on a hill. And a pumpkeeper had written it in 2604, in brown ink, with his needles standing up. Not dark. Nothing.

segments.expected: She made herself take it away again and think like somebody who had been brought up over an instrument shop.
segments.transcript: She made herself take it away again and think like somebody who had been brought up over an instrument shop.

segments.expected: "It's a second pin." She went pink. "The thumb was lifting. On the third, when the wax is hard. It was letting the first turn go."
segments.transcript: It's a second pin. She went pink. The thumb was lifting. On the third, when the wax is hard. It was letting the first turn go.

segments.expected: "What's there. All of it. What I do with my knees and where I look and which hand I use, and when. The things that I'd not think to say, because I've done them since before you were born." He set a stitch. "And you'll not get that by looking for mistakes. You got the thumb because you weren't looking for one. Go and do that for two months."
segments.transcript: What's there? All of it. What I do with my knees and where I look and which hand I use and when. The things that I'd not think to say because I've done them since before you were born. He set a stitch. And you'll not get that by looking for mistakes. You got the thumb because you weren't looking for one. Go and do that for two months.

segments.expected: "Watch if you like," she said. "You'll not learn anything. It's only folding."
segments.transcript: Watch if you like, she said. You'll not learn anything. It's only folding.
